chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Just as the beginning of every blessing is from Allah, the Mighty and High, which He has bestowed upon you, so too is the good from yourselves, even if it flows through Divine Decree.
ai.seo_question: What is the source of good and evil according to Imam al-Sadiq in this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the nuance of *al-Jabr wa al-Tafwid* by distinguishing the source of blessings from the source of evil, attributing the latter to human agency even when it unfolds through Divine Decree (*Qadr*). This hadith underscores the Shia doctrine of *Amr bayn al-Amrayn* (a matter between the two extremes), affirming that while God’s will encompasses all events, human free will is the primary locus for the manifestation of evil and the responsibility for it. It serves as a critical theological counter to strict predestination, emphasizing moral accountability within the framework of divine omniscience.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 6. My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) both said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-`Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn `Imran al-Ash`ari, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of `Ali ibn Ma`bad, on the authority of `Umar ibn Udhaynah, on the authority of Zurarah that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:
“Every bounty begins with Allah, the Mighty and High, who has bestowed it upon you. Every evil which befalls you is from yourselves, although the Divine Decrees flows in it.”
